Compare survey estimates between domains

Source: R/survey.R
survey_compare.Rd

Each domain's estimate against a reference domain: the difference, its standard error from the design (the covariance between the two estimates included, which is what a pair of separate intervals leaves out), a confidence interval and a two-sided p-value from the normal approximation.

Usage

survey_compare(
  design,
  data,
  y,
  by,
  stat = c("mean", "total", "proportion", "ratio"),
  denominator = NULL,
  levels = NULL,
  ref = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95
)

Arguments

design

A survey_design() built on data.

data

The data frame the design was built on.

y

The analysis column.

by

The domain columns to compare across.

stat

"mean", "total", "proportion" or "ratio" (of y to denominator).

denominator

For a ratio, the denominator column.

levels

For a proportion, the categories to report (default all observed).

ref

The reference domain, as its label (for several by columns, the labels joined with " / "); default the first.

conf_level

Confidence level.

Value

A data frame of class rmbl_svy_compare: domain, level (for a proportion), estimate, reference, difference, se, lower, upper, p_value.

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(region = rep(c("north", "south", "east"), length.out = 150),
                smoker = rbinom(150, 1, 0.3), w = runif(150, 50, 150))
des <- survey_design(d, weights = "w")
survey_compare(des, d, "smoker", by = "region", stat = "proportion",
               levels = "1", ref = "north")
#> Survey proportion of smoker against north (95% interval)
#>  domain level estimate reference difference      se   lower   upper p_value
#>    east     1   0.2538    0.3701    -0.1164 0.09485 -0.3023 0.06954  0.2199
#>   south     1   0.2352    0.3701    -0.1350 0.09464 -0.3205 0.05052  0.1538
